newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sugar ships hit by 24-hour strike at Brazil Santos.
newsitem.headline: Sugar ships hit by 24-hour strike at Brazil Santos.

text.p: Loading of sugar vessels in public terminals at Brazil's Santos port had halted due to a 24 hour strike by administrative portworkers which began at 0700 local/0900 GMT today, a CODESP port authority spokesman said.
"The port is virtually at a halt," the spokesman said.
"Of the 34 ships docked in CODESP terminals, only four vessels are loading liquid chemicals," he said.
Five ships docked in private terminals were operating normally, he added.
Some 13 ships were docked to load sugar in the port's public terminals, the spokesman said.
A further two vessels had been taking on soymeal and two ships were unloading wheat.
The portworkers are holding the strike in protest at a decision to open up the port's container terminal to leasing by the private sector.
Under an agreement with the former Transport Minister Odacir Klein, unions had been led to believe they would be involved in any decisions of this kind.

The portworkers are to stage a protest at 1500 local/1700 GMT this afternoon at the first public audience on the container terminal privatisation, said Bento Marques Prazeres, a director of the Portworkers' Union.
Although no further stoppages are planned, much will depend on on-going negotiations with the port authority, he said.
"The possibility of more strikes can't be ruled out," he said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
